newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates dip as notes mature.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates dip as notes mature.

text.p: *Banks want to stay liquid for the holidays
- Philippine interbank call loan rates dipped to an average of 10.90625 percent on Tuesday from 10.9375 following the maturity of 2.4 billion pesos worth of Treasury notes, dealers said.
The Central Bank, however, kept rates almost steady because it was borrowing funds at an overnight rate of 10.75 percent.
There were 31 lenders and 27 borrowers. Volume rose to 30.225 billion from 26.374 billion pesos.
"Banks are just staying square. They just want to be liquid as much as possible in view of the upcoming Christmas holidays," a dealer said.
She added banks have been trying to sell their short-term T-bills in the secondary market but most buyers favoured the two-year and five-year notes where rates are more attractive.
Investors prefer long-term notes because of a likely fall in interest rates following the planned two percentage-point reduction in reserve requirements next year, dealers said.
One dealer said the five-year notes had been sold at 13.5 percent and two years at 12.70 percent.

Meanwhile, a Reuters survey of nine financial institutions showed that three-month bills were being offered at 11.40 to 11.475 percent; six-month at 11.60 to 11.75; and one-year at 12.0 to 12.125 percent.
